newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco bourse ends year on optimistic note.
newsitem.headline: Morocco bourse ends year on optimistic note.

text.p: The Casablanca stock exchange closed on Tuesday 0.21 percent higher, ending on an optimistic note the year during which the index registered a 30.74 percent annual rise, brokers said.
The all-share index closed at 447.13 from 446.21 points on Monday. The exchange will be closed on Wednesday, a public holiday.
"The market remains globally bullish with an index registering a 30.74 percent progression during the year," Youssef Benkirane, analyst at Casablanca-based Maroc Inter Titres, told Reuters.
Morocco's largest private conglomerate, ONA closed at 521 dirhams, up six dirhams from Monday.
ONA has diversified stakes in more than 100 companies and a capitalisation of more than 8.3 billion dirhams.

Wafabank, a liquid stock that recently merged with Spanish Uniban bank, gained two dirhams to 552 dirhams. Banque Commerciale du Maroc, the market's largest capitalisation, was up three dirhams to close at 692 dirhams, traders said. Credit firm Eqdom Credit, which announced a capital increase recently, fell 23 dirhams to trade at 762 dirhams.
"The stock has been technically adjusted in the two last days, but this drop is not significant, we do not expect it to last," Benkirane said.
Eqdom, Morocco's first consumer credit company, was set up in 1974 by holding company Societe Nationale d'Investissement and major insurance companies.
Dairy company, Centrale Laitiere, an offshoot of ONA holding, was up 20 dirhams to close at 1,820 dirhams. The French firm Danone has a 20 percent stake in Centrale Laitiere.
"This value is rising ahead of the publication of company results which are expected to be good after it registered losses in 1995," Benkirane said.
Traded volume on the official market was 31.4 million dirhams from 23.3 million dirhams on Monday.
